# Chinese Technical Writing Guide , strip AI tone, enforce typography rules

Curated by Skill Harbor: style rules for writing Chinese technical documentation that reads like a senior engineer wrote it: plain, concrete, short sentences. One idea per sentence, active voice, facts instead of adjectives ("p99 latency dropped from 120 ms to 40 ms", not "performance greatly improved"), paragraphs that open with their point, and strict CJK typography (full-width punctuation, spacing between CJK and Latin, correct quotes and ellipses). The heart of it is an AI-tone checklist to run line by line against every draft: kill the stock openers and closers, the "not A but B" contrasts, the triple adjectives, the hype words, the jargon. by @leter, listed here with credit to its creator. Honest caveats: the skill content is written in Chinese and targets Chinese-language docs; also ships a typography reference and a manual-structure reference to read when those topics come up. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via GitHub.
